record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.original_question: For output feedback, determine when one can assign the closed-loop poles to a prescribed region or to prescribed locations in the left half-plane by choosing suitable feedback gains. The source emphasizes that, unlike the full-state-feedback case, output-feedback pole placement is still essentially unsolved even though partial results are known.

evidence.quote: A refinement of the stabilizability problem is the pole (i.e., eigenvalue) assignability problem. In this problem the goal is to determine feedback gains that place the closed-loop spectrum within a specified region or at specified locations in the left half plane.

In the output-feedback case, however, controllability and pole placement are not equivalent. Although this problem is essentially unsolved, some partial results are available [1, 17, 26, 30, 45, 49, 71, 78].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a linear time-invariant control system
  x'(t) = A x(t) + B u(t),   y(t) = C x(t),
where A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, B ∈ ℝ^{n×m}, C ∈ ℝ^{p×n}, and the pair (A,B) is controllable and (A,C) is observable. A static output feedback law u(t) = K y(t) with K ∈ ℝ^{m×p} produces the closed-loop matrix A + B K C, whose spectrum (multiset of eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity) is denoted σ(A + B K C) ⊂ ℂ.

Two output-feedback pole assignment problems are posed:

(a) (Pointwise assignment.) Given a self-conjugate multiset Λ = {λ_1, …, λ_n} ⊂ ℂ with each Re λ_i < 0, give verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on (A,B,C,Λ) for the existence of K ∈ ℝ^{m×p} such that σ(A + B K C) = Λ, and, when such K exists, provide a constructive procedure to compute it.

(b) (Regional assignment.) Given an open region Ω ⊂ ℂ contained in the open left half-plane and symmetric with respect to the real axis, give verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on (A,B,C,Ω) for the existence of K ∈ ℝ^{m×p} such that σ(A + B K C) ⊂ Ω, and, when such K exists, provide a constructive procedure to compute it.

Determine these conditions and procedures in full generality (i.e., for all n, m, p ≥ 1), going beyond the known sufficient dimensional conditions such as n ≤ m + p − 1.
artifact.status_search_result: Output-feedback pole assignment is widely described in the control-theory literature as a longstanding open problem. Surveys on static output feedback note that, despite many partial results (e.g., generic assignability when n ≤ m + p − 1, and algebro-geometric criteria), no general verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions or efficient algorithmic solutions are known.
